newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES FIRE GENERAL MANAGER MUCKLER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES FIRE GENERAL MANAGER MUCKLER.

text.p: Buffalo Sabres general manager John Muckler lost his feud with coach Ted Nolan and his job on Wednesday as the National Hockey League team dismissed him.
Muckler has had a rocky relationship with Nolan, who succeeded him as coach before the start of the 1995-96 season.

In the end, former Oilers coach Muckler lost out to Nolan, an Adams Trophy finalist as coach of the year after taking a team of overachievers to the Northeast Division title this season despite little expectations.
Buffalo's season ended with a five-game, second-round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Flyers.
Nolan guided the team to a 40-30-12 record this season and is 73-72-19 in his two years behind the bench using the young talent that Muckler stockpiled.

Muckler was 125-109-34 as Sabres coach and has an overall NHL coaching record of 206-197-60. He took over as Sabres coach in December 1991, after becoming director of hockey operations the previous summer.

Before joining Buffalo, Muckler coached the Edmonton Oilers for a pair of seasons, winning the 1990 Stanley Cup. An assistant coach with the Oilers in 1982, Muckler joined Glen Sather as co-coach for the 1985-86 season and helped guide the Edmonton dynasty of the 1980s.
